hero-announcement: Open beta — free while we build
hero-eyebrow: For teams publishing across more than one brand
hero-description: One calendar for planning, approvals, and publishing across all your profiles. Draft once, route with context, and launch together.
hero-note: Free while in beta. Billing is not switched on yet.
statement-problem-lead: Running content for several brands means the same week exists in five places at once —
statement-problem-emphasis: a spreadsheet for the plan, a chat thread for the approval, a folder for the assets, and someone's memory for what actually went out.
statement-problem-tail: Nothing is wrong until something is, and then nobody can say where it went wrong.
statement-answer-lead: PublyApp puts the whole week in one place:
statement-answer-emphasis: one calendar across every profile, one draft adapted per audience, and permissions that decide who may approve and who may publish, per action rather than per role.
statement-answer-tail: Every post carries its own record of who wrote it, who approved it, and when it went live.
tour-description: Move from draft to publish with one timeline, one approval flow, and one source of truth.
tour-tab-calendar-title: Calendar that follows every brand in one week
tour-tab-calendar-description: A single timeline gives your team a shared view of planned and queued content, per profile and per region, without opening another tool.
tour-tab-composer-title: Build one draft, shape one version per audience
tour-tab-composer-description: Reuse copy and assets across profiles, then adapt only what changes for a channel or brand voice.
tour-tab-approvals-title: No silent publishing, no guessing, no surprises
tour-tab-approvals-description: Approvals and publish permissions are clear at every step, so no one can move a post without the right sign-off.
tour-tab-profiles-title: Profile-level controls for every client account
tour-tab-profiles-description: Store each account profile once, manage membership and permissions by profile, and keep context clean when teams grow.
tour-tab-dashboards-title: See what moved and what is still waiting
tour-tab-dashboards-description: Use a single weekly view or cross-profile summary to review pacing, execution, and pending work at a glance.
facts-1-body: A single calendar replaces profile-by-profile planning, across every brand you run.
facts-3-body: Every post keeps its draft, approval and publish trail.
facts-4-body: Planned and queued content across every profile and region in a single shared timeline.
facts-5-body: Each client account profile is stored once, with its own membership and permissions, so contexts never bleed.
facts-6-body: Cross-profile summaries of pacing, execution and what is still waiting on someone.
who-for-title: Built for the work that does not fit in one inbox
who-for-teams-agencies-body: Invite colleagues quickly, keep client profiles isolated, and keep context stable across handovers.
who-for-inhouse-operations-body: Keep weekly planning close to your core team while still allowing delegated approvals and publishing.
who-for-small-studios-body: Use a lightweight flow before you scale teams or tools, with room to grow into heavier operations.
who-for-role-access-body: Draft, approve, and publish permissions stay scoped by profile and are easy to adjust per team need.
who-for-shared-queue-body: Drafts enter a single workflow and move visibly across review stages. No silent edits from outside the process.
approvals-body: Approving and publishing are separate, explicit permissions, granted per action rather than bundled into a role. A teammate can draft without being able to publish; a client contact can approve without gaining access to anyone else's profile. Every state change keeps its author and its timestamp, so the history of a post is the post.
chain-1-body: Write once, then adapt only what a channel or a brand voice actually requires.
chain-2-body: Route to whoever holds the approval permission for that profile. Nothing moves without it.
chain-3-body: Publishing is its own permission, and the post keeps the whole trail behind it.
trial-step-1-description: Create your first profile and invite your team members.
trial-step-2-description: Start weekly planning with approvals in place and shared queue habits established.
trial-step-3-description: Keep the same rhythm with less back-and-forth and cleaner handoffs.
trial-plan-note: The free trial is planned before general availability. Today, PublyApp is free while in beta.
pricing-studio-description: Two brand profiles, three people, one shared calendar.
pricing-agency-description: Ten profiles, per-action permissions and approvals, full history.
faq-title: Questions teams ask at first look
faq-0-question: Can I run this alongside another scheduling tool?
faq-0-answer: Yes. Teams usually run both for a short period while they move workflows. You can keep an external tool connected while shifting teams over profile by profile.
faq-1-question: What does onboarding require before I can draft?
faq-1-answer: You need one project team and one profile, then your workflow settings and approvals can be added in the same screen.
faq-2-answer: Approvals are first-class actions in the post lifecycle. Every change keeps context and the history of who approved it.
faq-3-question: What support is available if I get stuck?
faq-3-answer: Today, PublyApp is free while in beta, but no trial support flow is active yet. A free trial is planned before general availability; its support terms have not been published.
closing-description: One plan. One calendar. One set of approvals. Today, PublyApp is free while in beta; a lightweight free trial is planned before general availability.
